## Socaire in Atacama: a village on the way to the high-altitude lagoons

Socaire is a small Andean settlement in northern [Chile](/chile/), southeast of [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The road to the famous high-altitude Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons passes through this area. For many travellers, Socaire is a stop on the way uphill, but the village is also worth discovering as a place where the culture of the desert highlands remains very much alive.

Stone and adobe buildings, small plots of farmland and arid mountain scenery characterise the village. Local traditions are associated with the Lickanantay, or Atacameño, people. Socaire is therefore more than a convenient place for lunch or changing vehicles: it has its own history, economy and community, which helps manage the surrounding natural areas.

## Where is Socaire, and why stop here?

Socaire lies on Route 23 south of San Pedro de Atacama and [Toconao](/chile/place/toconao/). Regional tourism sources place it about 86 km from San Pedro. The road continues to the high-altitude lagoons, which sit above 4,100 metres. The village itself is at more than 3,000 metres, a notable change in altitude from San Pedro and the Atacama Salt Flat.

Stopping here breaks up a long sightseeing day, provides a glimpse of life in a small Andean community and gives travellers an opportunity to assess how they feel before ascending farther. A brief stop, however, is not a substitute for proper acclimatisation: people respond to altitude differently.

## Terraces, church and local culture

Agricultural terraces around Socaire preserve traditions of mountain-water management and farming. Crops suited to local conditions, including maize and quinoa, have been grown here for generations and continue to be cultivated. The fields and stone structures reveal how communities have lived in these dry highlands over time.

The village has a historic church connected with local religious and community traditions. When an itinerary includes Socaire, a short visit should respect private courtyards, agricultural plots and areas closed to visitors.

Local culture is alive. Travellers learn more by listening to residents and guides than by treating the village as an uninhabited museum. Specific craft activities, meetings with residents and visits to homes require separate arrangements.

## Miscanti and Miñiques: what lies beyond Socaire?

For many excursions, the main natural destinations are [Miscanti Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-miscanti/) and [Miñiques Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-miniques/). Their deep-blue waters lie among volcanic slopes. They form part of the high-altitude Los Flamencos protected area, so visiting rules differ from those for a walk along a village road.

The scenery is strikingly contrasting: pale dry ground, mountain slopes and deeply coloured water. You may observe characteristic high-altitude wildlife, although trail access, conditions and bird behaviour depend on the season and conservation regulations. Passing through Socaire does not itself guarantee visits to both lagoons: the programme and confirmed access determine that.

The local community is among those involved in managing visits to nearby natural sites. Ticket booking and check-in arrangements may change. The official Socaire Chile resource describes advance reservations and access checks at Socaire, so it is best to arrange lagoon visits before leaving San Pedro.

## Altitude and physical wellbeing

The route to the lagoons climbs above 4,000 metres. Even an ordinary walk at this altitude feels different from one at sea level. It is often necessary to slow down, drink enough water and pay close attention to how you feel. If you develop a marked headache, nausea, dizziness or shortness of breath, tell your guide and do not force yourself to continue ascending; decisions about medical assistance and descent depend on your condition.

The sun is intense in Atacama, while high-altitude winds can be cold. Bring warm layers, sunglasses, a hat and drinking water. Road conditions and individual medical restrictions should be considered before the trip, especially if ascending rapidly from lower elevations.

## Socaire on an Atacama excursion

A sightseeing day can combine several neighbouring natural areas. For example, the route may begin at [Miscanti](/chile/place/laguna-miscanti/) and [Miñiques](/chile/place/laguna-miniques/) lagoons, continue through Socaire and head to the [Atacama Salt Flat](/chile/place/atacama-salt-flat/) and [Chaxa Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-chaxa/). The actual sequence depends on access hours, weather and the chosen trip format.

| Stop | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Socaire | Culture and a break |
| Miscanti | High-altitude lake |
| Miñiques | Lagoon near a volcano |
| Chaxa | Birds and salt flat |

If time is limited, it is better to devote attention to one complete high-altitude outing than to add several distant attractions without allowing for travel times. Socaire neatly connects the natural and cultural aspects of such a journey.

## Socaire on Ada Tours itineraries

Our [9-day Hidden Treasures of Chile tour](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) includes a day visiting Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons, stopping at Socaire and continuing to the Atacama Salt Flat and Toconao. The current itinerary includes lunch in Socaire and admission tickets to the high-altitude lagoons and Chaxa Lagoon. These services are confirmed for this particular tour; other itineraries may have different conditions.

When comparing [our tours of Chile](/chile/tour/), check how much time they allot to Atacama, what altitude they reach and which individual visits are included. The words San Pedro de Atacama in a tour title do not, by themselves, mean an excursion to Socaire or both lagoons.

## Frequently asked questions about Socaire

### Where is Socaire?

In the Antofagasta Region, southeast of San Pedro de Atacama. The village is on the way to the high-altitude Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons.

### Are Socaire and the Miscanti lagoons the same place?

No. Socaire is a settlement, while the lagoons lie farther away in the highlands. Visiting the village does not replace an excursion to the lakes.

### Do you need to book a lagoon visit in advance?

High-altitude natural sites have advance booking procedures and access checks through the official operator. Confirm the current procedure, times and availability before departure.

### Why should you take altitude into account after Socaire?

The road continues climbing to lagoons above 4,100 metres. Even an easy walk requires attention to your wellbeing, weather and prior acclimatisation.

## Tours through Socaire: choosing a route to the Atacama lagoons

[Socaire](/chile/place/socaire/) is a settlement near [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) where Ada Tours programmes stop on the way to the high-altitude lagoons. A single sightseeing day can include mountain plateaus, lake waters and white salt-flat landscapes. The village itself, however, is only one part of the route. The real differences between the tours are in what happens before and after Atacama.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Socaire on their main itineraries. There are short journeys around northern Chile as well as longer trips continuing to Patagonia, Easter Island and other South American countries. Choose by the number of full days, geographical scope and complexity of transfers rather than by one stop.

## What a day visiting Socaire includes

Common destinations include [Miscanti Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-miscanti/), [Miñiques Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-miniques/), the [Atacama Salt Flat](/chile/place/atacama-salt-flat/), [Chaxa Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-chaxa/) and [Toconao](/chile/place/toconao/). These places differ substantially. Miscanti and Miñiques lie high in the mountains, while Chaxa is in the salt basin and known for birdwatching. The day therefore involves changes in altitude and several long road sections.

On the [12-day Best of Chile tour](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/), visits to Miscanti and Miñiques are followed by lunch in Socaire, then the salt flat and Chaxa. The [9-day Hidden Treasures of Chile itinerary](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) likewise confirms lunch at Socaire and tickets to the lagoons. **Included services vary between programmes:** do not assume that the terms of one tour apply to another because both visit the same place.

## Short and long tours through Socaire

| Duration | What complements Atacama |
|---|---|
| 6 days | Santiago, Valparaíso |
| 7 days | Patagonia |
| 9 days | Marble Caves, glaciers |
| 12 days | Patagonia, Easter Island |

[Chile: An Otherworldly Journey on Earth](/chile/tour/chile-otherworldly-journey/) lasts 6 days. It combines Atacama with Santiago, Valparaíso and Viña del Mar. The day visiting the high-altitude lakes includes a stop in Socaire and a lunch of local dishes. It introduces northern Chile without extensive travel to the far south.

The [7-day tour of Santiago, Atacama and Torres del Paine](/chile/tour/chile-santiago-atacama-torres-del-paine/) adds [Patagonian scenery](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). It suits those who want two completely different natural regions, provided they are comfortable with flights and a busy itinerary rather than spending extra time in any one place.

The [9-day Hidden Treasures of Chile](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) includes the northern desert, [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/), [San Rafael Glacier](/chile/place/san-rafael-glacier/) and Patagonia. Much of the journey is devoted to natural regions beyond the standard Santiago–Atacama combination.

The [12-day Best of Chile tour](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/) combines the lagoons with Patagonia and [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/). If you are interested in Rapa Nui culture as well as mountain and desert landscapes, this route offers greater variety. It also requires more time for flights.

On [VIP Chile 5*](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/), the high-altitude lagoon excursion forms part of a 10-day itinerary through northern and southern Chile. The VIP label does not itself guarantee any particular service: accommodation, guides, tickets and meals must be checked against what this programme includes.

## Altitude, weather and organising the excursion

The high-altitude lagoons require preparation even when travelling by car. Pack warm layers, sun protection and water: wind and temperature changes are more noticeable in the mountains. If you are sensitive to altitude, discuss the stop sequence, pace and conditions with the organiser in advance. Thin air can affect how you feel irrespective of physical exertion.

Access to Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons is regulated through a local advance-booking and check-in system in Socaire. Rules and check-in hours change, so check them before departure. Buying an excursion does not automatically mean every admission ticket and special permit is included in the price unless the chosen tour explicitly says so.

When choosing dates, consider seasonal conditions in Atacama and the other regions on your route. Good weather in Santiago does not mean the same conditions in the highlands or Patagonia. Ada Tours helps organise the sequence of regions and prepare for different climates.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Socaire

### Is Socaire a destination in its own right or a stop?

On the itineraries listed here, it is primarily a stop on the way to the high-altitude lagoons. Exploring the settlement in depth requires separate arrangements.

### Can you see Miscanti, Miñiques and the salt flat on one day?

Yes. Such excursion days feature in current programmes. The route is long, however, and the order of stops, lunch and admission tickets differ.

### Which tour should I choose if Atacama is my main interest?

Start with the [6-day Otherworldly Journey on Earth](/chile/tour/chile-otherworldly-journey/). If you also want Patagonia, compare it with the [7-day tour](/chile/tour/chile-santiago-atacama-torres-del-paine/) or longer itineraries.

### Must lagoon visits be booked in advance?

Regulated natural areas have procedures for booking and checking tickets in advance. Confirm the current details before travelling, separately from the ordinary stop in Socaire.

## Tahai on Easter Island: three oceanfront platforms with moai

**Tahai** is an archaeological complex on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), also known as Rapa Nui. Its distinctive feature is several ceremonial *ahu* platforms bearing moai statues near the open ocean coast. Here, it is especially clear how the monuments relate not only to individual stone figures, but to the layout of the entire sacred space.

Tahai is near [Hanga Roa](/chile/place/hanga-roa/). It is a convenient introduction to Rapa Nui heritage before travelling to the island's other monuments. Visits must nevertheless follow current national park regulations and guiding requirements.

## The three ahu and their stone statues

The complex includes **Vai Uri, Tahai and Ko Te Riku** platforms. A group of moai remains on the first, while the other two display individual restored sculptures. The Ko Te Riku moai stands out for its reconstructed eyes and red stone headdress.

This is not a modern ornamental arrangement. The statues and platforms are part of the ancient Rapa Nui people's heritage, connected with ancestral veneration and ceremonies. Archaeologists restored the complex in the late 1960s, as documented in Chilean cultural heritage records. Photographs therefore show both surviving monuments and the results of archaeological restoration.

The site also contains remains of dwellings and other structures. Understanding the platforms' position relative to the shore and settlement is an important part of visiting.

## How Tahai differs from other places on Rapa Nui

[Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) is known for its long restored platform with fifteen moai. [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is associated with the quarries where the statues were carved from tuff. Tahai's main attraction is three ceremonial platforms within a single space, set beside the coast.

| Place | What it helps explain |
|---|---|
| Tahai | The layout of a ceremonial complex |
| [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) | Large restored platforms |
| [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) | How moai were made |
| [Hanga Roa](/chile/place/hanga-roa/) | Modern life on the island |

## Tahai on an Ada Tours itinerary

On our current [Colourful Santiago and Mysterious Easter Island tour](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/), Tahai is visited on the same excursion day as Ahu Akivi and the Puna Pau quarry. The programme explicitly names Tahai's three platforms, followed by a flight from the island to Santiago. The itinerary connects the main archaeological themes of Rapa Nui without confusing separate monuments as a single place.

On a trip lasting several days, divide archaeological site visits to leave enough time for the guide's explanations and observation from permitted points.

## What to know before visiting

The moai and stonework are protected cultural heritage. Climbing statues or platforms, crossing barriers and touching the monuments are prohibited. Wind and strong sun on the exposed coast make water, a hat and comfortable shoes useful.

Tahai is known for its evening light beside the ocean, but appealing lighting does not override the visiting rules. Check access at the desired hour with your trip organiser and park administration.

## Frequently asked questions about Tahai

### Is Tahai a single moai statue?

No. It is an archaeological complex with three main platforms and several statues.

### What makes the Ko Te Riku moai distinctive?

It is known for its reconstructed eyes and a red stone headdress.

### Can Tahai be combined with other island monuments?

Yes. One of our current tours visits Tahai alongside Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau.

### Are there special rules for the site?

Yes. It is a protected archaeological monument, with current access and guiding determined by Rapa Nui National Park regulations.

## Tours visiting Tahai on Easter Island

[Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/) is a ceremonial complex on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), beside the coast near [Hanga Roa](/chile/place/hanga-roa/). According to Rapa Nui National Park, the complex includes three restored ahu platforms and remains of an ancient settlement. Tahai is especially renowned for its views of moai and the ocean in the evening light.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Tahai on the main itinerary. In most cases, it is one of several archaeological monuments visited on an excursion day. Choose your trip according to how thoroughly it explores Rapa Nui culture and how much time remains on the island.

## Combining Tahai with other monuments

Tahai is often visited together with [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) and the [Puna Pau quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/). Ahu Akivi is known for restored moai, while Puna Pau supplied red volcanic stone for the pukao headdresses. These places reveal different stages in the creation and use of the island's monuments.

Another excursion day may combine the [Rano Raraku quarry](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) and [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/). Moai were carved at Rano Raraku, fifteen restored statues stand at Tongariki, and archaeological sites sit beside the sandy beach at Anakena. [Orongo](/chile/place/orongo-village/) introduces another island ceremonial tradition.

**An itinerary is about more than the number of statues you see.** Consider how many aspects of island history the excursions explore, whether a guide is provided and whether free time remains after a full day.

## Three days on Rapa Nui: the essentials

[Easter Island: Three Days Among Moai and Volcanoes](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/) is a dedicated island programme. The first day includes arrival and Orongo; the second explores the south coast, Rano Raraku, Tongariki and Anakena. Day 3 features a 4-hour private excursion with an English-speaking guide to Ahu Akivi, Ahu Hanga Pukure, Puna Pau and Tahai, followed by an airport transfer.

It suits travellers who want to devote a short trip entirely to Rapa Nui. Several major monuments can be visited without adding excursions on mainland Chile. The departure day's schedule depends on the transfer time, however, which should be matched to the actual flight.

## Tahai on itineraries through Santiago and other regions

[Colourful Santiago and Mysterious Easter Island](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/) lasts 6 days. Before island excursions, travellers visit Santiago, Valparaíso and Viña del Mar. On Rapa Nui, Tahai is included on a day with Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau. This format suits those wanting both the capital and the island without an extremely long trip around Chile.

The [12-day Best of Chile tour](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/) adds the Atacama Desert and [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) to island archaeology. It allows travellers to compare northern high-altitude scenery, Patagonia and Polynesian culture, but requires domestic flights.

The [17-day Chile and Argentina Grand Tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) covers even more: alongside Rapa Nui it includes Atacama, Patagonia, wine regions, Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires. Assess not only time at Tahai but the overall sequence of regions and the number of transfers.

Tahai also features in the [33-day journey through Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/), although the island visit is just one part of a major South American adventure. If your main interest is Rapa Nui archaeology, a shorter dedicated island trip is generally more practical.

| Main objective | Format to consider |
|---|---|
| Rapa Nui only | Three days on the island |
| Island and capital | Santiago + Rapa Nui |
| Different regions of Chile | Atacama, Patagonia, island |
| Multiple countries | Extended South American itinerary |

## What to check before booking

Compare the day visiting Tahai with other island excursions. If it is scheduled at the end of a day with several stops, there may be little time for independent photographs. Do not assume sunset at Tahai is a guaranteed part of the trip unless the visiting time is specifically stated.

Rapa Nui National Park sets rules for visiting protected sites, buying admission tickets and using accredited guides. Before travelling, confirm which sites are covered and how the current park requirements will be met. Stay on permitted paths; touching moai and crossing barriers are prohibited.

For longer itineraries, check flights and connections separately. Easter Island is remote from mainland Chile, so one additional flight has a greater impact on the total duration of travel than a short overland excursion.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Tahai

### Can you see Tahai on a short tour?

Yes. It is included on the final day of the [3-day Easter Island trip](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/).

### Are Tahai and Ahu Tongariki the same complex?

No. [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/) is near Hanga Roa, while [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) is a separate large ceremonial platform elsewhere on the island. Some tours visit them on different days.

### Do all itineraries include sunset at Tahai?

No. Tahai is known for its beautiful evening light, but only a visiting time confirmed by the specific itinerary counts as an included activity.

### Should you choose three days or a longer Chile tour?

For a focused introduction to the island's monuments, choose the [3-day itinerary](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/). If you also want Atacama and Patagonia, compare it with the [12-day Chile tour](/chile/tour/best-of-chile-easter-island-12-days/).

## San Lucas Church and Toconao's bell tower: architecture of an Atacama oasis

In the small village of [Toconao](/chile/place/toconao/), near the Atacama Salt Flat, stand San Lucas Church and a separate stone bell tower. Against the dry desert, these structures look striking: pale stone blocks, clearly defined tiers of the tower, a small square and traditional houses offer a completely different view from the panoramas of lagoons and volcanoes.

**Toconao's bell tower is an official Historic Monument of Chile**, entered in the national register in 1951. Together with the church, it tells the story of Lickanantay architecture, colonial religious tradition and daily life in the oasis. It is one of the stops that make an [Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) itinerary richer than a sequence of natural sights.

## Where is Toconao?

Toconao lies in Chile's Antofagasta Region, near the northeastern edge of the [Atacama Salt Flat](/chile/place/atacama-salt-flat/). A road connects it with [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), the starting point for numerous trips to the salt flat and high-altitude lagoons.

The environment is arid, yet the oasis has water sources and patches of green vegetation. Agriculture and crafts have therefore long been important to local life. Stopping at the main square shows how people settled at the edge of the desert: buildings use local materials, and the church remains part of a living community.

According to Chile's Council of National Monuments, Toconao stands at approximately 2,475 metres above sea level. This is markedly lower than some of Atacama's high-altitude lagoons and geysers, but its sun and dry air still require care.

## Why is the bell tower separate from the church?

A free-standing belfry is a characteristic feature of several historic churches in the Andean region. In Toconao, the tower stands beside the church but is not joined to the main building. Seen from the square, they appear as separate architectural parts of one complex.

The tower was built of worked local stone using traditional bonding materials. According to Chile's Council of National Monuments, it has **three progressively narrowing tiers**, divided by prominent cornices. A dome-shaped feature made of cactus wood crowns the upper section.

Unlike large urban cathedrals, this building is distinguished by precise proportions and the handling of simple materials. You can appreciate its construction by walking through the square on permitted routes: different angles reveal its tiers, stonework and distance from the church.

## What stone was used for the buildings?

Toconao's buildings are known for their use of **liparite**, a local volcanic stone suitable for carving and shaping. It was quarried nearby and used for homes and handicrafts as well as religious buildings.

San Lucas Church was constructed in the 18th century; the official register dates it to **1744**. The church and tower reveal how European ecclesiastical architecture was adapted to local construction traditions and the conditions of a desert settlement.

The value of the ensemble lies in its materials: the texture of stone blocks, restrained façades and proximity to ordinary village buildings. It reveals Atacama as a place with community history, not merely a collection of volcanoes and coloured lagoons.

## Why does the bell tower have protected status?

The tower was designated a monument by Decree No. 5058 of 1951. This recognises its historical and architectural value at the national level. Heritage protection should not be mistaken for a guarantee of unrestricted access to the church interior or the tower.

The church remains connected with the local community's life. Toconao's traditional events include the feast of Saint Luke, the village's patron saint. Respect the religious setting: speak quietly during services, seek permission for indoor photography and stay out of closed areas.

## What to see nearby

Toconao combines well with natural stops in the southern part of the San Pedro region. Routes often pass the [Atacama Salt Flat](/chile/place/atacama-salt-flat/) and [Chaxa Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-chaxa/), where the salt landscape and birdwatching are the main attractions. Longer excursions may include [Miscanti Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-miscanti/) and [Miñiques Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-miniques/).

These stops complement one another. The lagoons and salt flat introduce the area's geography and nature, while the church and bell tower tell the story of people living in the desert. That is why a short stop in Toconao deserves time, even when nature is the day's primary focus.

| Stop | What to see |
|---|---|
| San Lucas | Historic church |
| Bell tower | Three-tiered tower |
| [Chaxa](/chile/place/laguna-chaxa/) | Salt flat and birds |
| [Miscanti](/chile/place/laguna-miscanti/) | High-altitude lake |

## What is a visit like?

You can admire the bell tower from the square. Access to the church interior depends on opening hours, services and local rules. Climbing the tower should not be assumed to be an ordinary tourist option. A short exterior visit with time for photographs and an explanation of the construction is usually sufficient.

Atacama's strong sun can be felt even when air temperatures are moderate. Bring a hat, water, sunscreen and comfortable shoes for stone paths. For higher lagoons, warm clothing is also required, as daytime temperatures can vary significantly.

## Toconao on Ada Tours itineraries

Our [Hidden Treasures of Chile tour](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) includes a stop at Toconao during the day visiting high-altitude lagoons and the Atacama Salt Flat. The programme includes the [Chaxa Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-chaxa/) area, lunch in Socaire and a return to San Pedro. It names San Lucas Church and the bell tower as Toconao sights; it does not promise a climb up the tower.

Our [VIP Chile 5* itinerary](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/) also lists Toconao as a stop after the lagoons and salt flat. Compare guiding, transport and included services against each actual programme: VIP status says nothing about access to closed rooms.

For travellers planning around cultural monuments, see the [Culture and History journeys catalogue](/interests/culture-and-history/); for a trip specifically within Chile, also explore our [Chile tours](/chile/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about San Lucas Church

### When was San Lucas Church in Toconao built?

Chile's Council of National Monuments gives the year 1744. The neighbouring bell tower has been protected as a historic monument since 1951.

### Can you climb the bell tower?

Climbing is not a standard tourist service. The tower is generally viewed from the square, and additional access requires separate permission.

### Why are the buildings made of pale stone?

Toconao uses local volcanic stone called liparite. Shaped blocks were used to build homes and religious structures and make crafts.

### How is Toconao different from Machuca?

[Toconao](/chile/place/toconao/) is an oasis near the salt flat, while [Machuca](/chile/place/machuca/) is much higher in the mountains. Machuca also has a historic church, but the settlements' architecture and climate differ.
